name: Soil Moisture and Mud
description: Rain makes soil and grass muddy, causing wheel slippage and slower speeds. This creates a distinct high-travel-time mode during or after wet weather, especially on the grass of Path 2.

name: Crop Growth Stage
description: As crops grow taller, they can overhang Path 2, partially blocking the camera's field of view. This forces the robot to navigate more cautiously (slower) or trigger false obstacle detections compared to early-season clear paths.

name: Time of Day and Sun Position
description: Camera navigation is highly sensitive to lighting. Low sun angles (dawn/dusk) cause direct glare or long shadows, while night requires active lighting. These distinct lighting states create discrete travel-time profiles due to varying image processing delays.

name: Path Maintenance and Grass Height
description: On Path 2, tall, unmown grass increases rolling resistance and wheel slip, and can obscure ground-level obstacles. Travel times will cluster into two distinct modes: 'recently mown' (fast) and 'overgrown' (slow).

name: Farm Traffic and Obstacles
description: Path 1 (outer edge) is likely shared with human workers, tractors, or support vehicles. The presence of these obstacles causes the robot to stop, wait, or slow down, creating a multi-modal distribution (clear path vs. obstructed path).

name: Precipitation
description: Active rain or heavy fog directly degrades camera visibility (water droplets on the lens) and triggers safety-focused speed reductions in the navigation controller.

name: Harsh Shadows and Contrast
description: Strong, direct sunlight creates high-contrast shadows (especially on Path 2 under crop canopies). Vision algorithms often misidentify these shadows as physical obstacles, causing sudden decelerations and path-revalidation maneuvers.
relatedTo: Time of Day and Sun Position

name: Battery State of Charge and Health
description: The robot's controller may implement a 'low-power' or 'eco' mode that caps maximum motor output when the battery drops below a certain threshold, leading to a bimodal speed distribution.

name: Ambient and Motor Temperature
description: Extreme heat triggers thermal throttling of the onboard computers or drive motors to prevent damage, while extreme cold reduces battery efficiency. Both lead to distinct slow-travel modes.
relatedTo: Battery State of Charge and Health

name: Sensor Degradation
description: Dust, mud splashes, or pollen accumulating on the camera lenses over time reduces image contrast. This causes the navigation system to default to a slower, high-confidence processing mode until the lenses are cleaned.

name: GNSS Signal Quality
description: If the camera-based navigation is aided by GNSS, signal multipath or loss (e.g., under a dense canopy on Path 2 or near trees on Path 1) forces the robot to switch to slower, dead-reckoning safety modes.

name: Wind Speed and Crop Sway
description: High winds cause crops on Path 2 to sway into the robot's path dynamically. The vision system perceives this dynamic movement as transient obstacles, resulting in intermittent braking.

name: Route Surface Degradation
description: Potholes, ruts from heavy machinery, or loose gravel on Path 1 can emerge over the season. This causes high-vibration travel, forcing the robot's internal IMU safety limits to slow down the vehicle.

name: Robot Payload
description: If the robot carries variable payloads (e.g., carrying tools, full/empty water tanks for spraying, or collected samples), the added mass slows acceleration and speed, especially when climbing inclines.
relatedTo: Battery State of Charge and Health

name: Tire Wear and Inflation Pressure
description: Gradual loss of tire pressure or tread wear decreases traction on grass and dirt, leading to higher slippage rates that accumulate into distinct, longer travel times before maintenance events.
